answer: The premise appears to be incorrect. wvRN (weighted-vote relational neighbor, Macskassy & Provost) does not use a one-vs-rest logistic regression classifier. It is a non-parametric relational method: for each unlabeled node, it estimates class membership as a weighted average of the known or currently estimated labels of its neighbors, normalized by the total edge weight, and often iterates this update until the estimates stabilize. Because it has no learned model, it is not trained the way the logistic regression baselines are. Any statement that wvRN shares a one-vs-rest logistic regression classifier with other baselines would therefore be a mischaracterization, unless a specific paper defined its own variant that does so.
confidence_reasoning: I am fairly confident wvRN is a non-parametric weighted-vote method without a learned logistic regression, but I cannot verify the specific paper the question refers to, which might define a variant differently.

triples.target: weighted average of known or estimated neighbor labels normalized by total edge weight
